about: Independent check set for Step 14 (conversation_recall_plan.md G.16 Step 14), written after the first measurement and before any run of it. It is never used to choose a number; it only checks values chosen on the other sets. Every conversation is invented. 'speaker_name' and 'recorded_scope' are synthetic test annotations standing in for the stored name and permanent identity IDs; 'helper_query' is hand-written, no model wrote it.

messages.author: user
messages.text: I'm opening a tiny bakery stall at the Saturday market in April. I need help planning the menu, pricing and the setup.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Exciting. Start with five or six items you can bake reliably in one morning, price them from ingredient cost times three, and plan a table layout that keeps the cash box away from the front edge.

messages.author: user
messages.text: Menu decision: sourdough loaves, cardamom buns, rye crackers and lemon drizzle slices. Four items to start.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: A focused menu. Cardamom buns sell well in the morning, and lemon drizzle keeps for two days if it doesn't sell.

messages.author: user
messages.text: How often do I feed the sourdough starter if I bake only on Fridays?

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Keep the starter in the fridge during the week, feed it once on Sunday, and take it out Thursday morning for two feeds before the Friday bake.

messages.author: user
messages.text: The market manager says the stall fee is 35 euros a day and I need my own canopy, minimum 3 by 3 meters.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: A 3 by 3 meter canopy with weights on each leg is standard. Budget the 35 euro fee into your pricing: about seven buns' worth of profit.

messages.author: user
messages.text: What should I charge for the cardamom buns?

messages.author: ai
messages.text: With ingredients at about 70 cents a bun, 3 euros each or two for 5.50 is reasonable for a market.

messages.author: user
messages.text: I found a secondhand deck oven for 900 euros from a closing cafe in Linden Street.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: A deck oven is ideal for sourdough. Check the door seals and that the thermostat holds temperature before paying.

messages.author: user
messages.text: What labels do I legally need on the rye crackers?

messages.author: ai
messages.text: List the ingredients in descending weight, highlight allergens such as rye, gluten and sesame, give a best-before date and your business name and address.

messages.author: user
messages.text: Change of plan: I'm dropping the rye crackers. They take too long to roll. Replacing them with oat and honey cookies.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Oat and honey cookies are faster and keep well. Remember honey is not an allergen, but oats need a gluten warning if they are not certified gluten free.

messages.author: user
messages.text: my sister wants to help on the first saturday shes good with people but terrible with money

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Then give her the serving and talking, and you keep the cash box. A card reader also cuts down on handling change.

messages.author: user
messages.text: Which card reader works without a long contract?

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Pay-as-you-go readers with a flat fee per transaction and no monthly charge are best for a weekly stall. Make sure it works offline and syncs later, since market Wi-Fi is unreliable.

messages.author: user
messages.text: The deck oven fell through. The cafe sold it to someone else, so I'm renting time in a shared commercial kitchen on Friday nights instead.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: A shared kitchen also solves the food safety inspection, since it is already certified. Book a regular Friday slot so you're not competing for oven space.

messages.author: user
messages.text: How many sourdough loaves should I bake for the first market?

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Start with 20 loaves. Note what sells out by eleven and adjust the next week; it's better to sell out than to take bread home.

messages.author: user
messages.text: Pip, I've started learning the fiddle. My teacher gave me a reel called The Silver Spear for this week.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: The Silver Spear is a lovely first reel. Practise it slowly with a metronome at 60 before you try it at speed.

messages.author: user
messages.text: My bow keeps squeaking on the E string. Is it the rosin?

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Usually it's too little rosin or too much pressure near the fingerboard. Rosin the bow with a few long strokes and play a little closer to the bridge.

messages.author: user
messages.text: I played The Silver Spear all the way through at the session in the pub on Thursday. Nobody laughed!

messages.author: ai
messages.text: That's a real milestone. Playing in a session is the hardest part; after the first time it gets easier.

messages.author: user
messages.text: I'm switching my day job schedule to four long days so I have Fridays free for practice.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Four long days can work if you protect your evenings. Use Friday mornings for practice while you're fresh.

messages.author: user
messages.text: New hobby too: I'm building a bat box for the garden from untreated larch boards.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Larch is a good choice since it's durable without treatment. Mount the bat box at least four meters high, facing south or southeast.

messages.author: user
messages.text: The bat box is up on the gable wall. Now I just wait for bats.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: It can take a season or more for bats to move in. Check for droppings below it at the end of summer.

messages.author: user
messages.text: I saw two pipistrelles flying around the garden at dusk last night.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Pipistrelles are a great sign. They may be scouting the bat box already.

messages.author: user
messages.text: Ash unrolls her half-finished map on the inn table. 'I need a guide over the Hollow Pass before the snow closes it.'

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Ash the innkeeper wipes his hands on his apron. 'My nephew Corin knows the pass. He'll take you for a week's board and a copy of your map.'

messages.author: user
messages.text: Ash the cartographer agrees, and inks a small lantern symbol where the inn sits on the map.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: The innkeeper chuckles at the lantern. 'Put a warning by the old bridge too. Half its planks are rotten.'

messages.author: user
messages.text: On the second day, Ash finds a carved stone marker near the pass with a spiral and three lines. She copies it into her notebook.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: Corin goes pale at the spiral. 'That's the sign of the Hollow Folk. We camp below the ridge tonight, not on it.'

messages.author: user
messages.text: Back at the inn, Ash pays the innkeeper in silver and gives Corin the finished copy of the map.

messages.author: ai
messages.text: The innkeeper weighs the silver. 'Fair. And if the Hollow Folk ask, you never stayed here,' he says with a wink.
